title: Retry transient install transport loss in the same session; fail fast on deterministic errors
summary: Package installation is a separate failure plane. A live T4 job reached installation and returned RuntimeError: Connection was lost; destroying the whole allocation was unnecessarily brittle. The repaired adapter retries only recognizable transport failures in the same allocated session with bounded backoff. Dependency-resolution errors, bad package names, authorization errors and other deterministic install failures do not retry.
evidence_note: Live dev17 qualification: a simulated Connection was lost retried exactly once and then succeeded; a deterministic bad-package failure stopped immediately. The same behavior was then exercised in live Colab where installation retry worked and execution continued.
invariants: Retry classification is narrow and evidence-bearing.
A transport retry reuses the same named session if it is still alive.
Bound retries and backoff; never turn a deterministic packaging error into a long retry loop.
Record each attempt without exposing secret material.
